enonce.question:
Read about Fares.
Fares lives far from his school. He ______ (go) to school by bus. After school, he ______ (do) his homework and he ______ (watch) cartoons.

1) Complete with the present simple of the verbs in brackets.
2) Complete the rule: with he, she and it, verbs ending in -o, -ch, -sh, -ss or -x take ______.
3) Write the he / she / it form of: wash, play.
4) Write about you: I ______ to school by bus / by car / on foot.

Read about Meriem's morning.
Meriem is a pupil in Kairouan. She ______ (get) up at 7 o'clock. She ______ (eat) breakfast with her family. Then she ______ (walk) to school with her friends.

1) Put the verbs in brackets in the present simple.
2) What do we add to the verb with he, she and it?
3) Write about you: I ______ up at ______ o'clock.

Read about Anis and Malek's weekend.
On Saturday, Anis and Malek play football in the park. They watch a film in the evening. On Sunday they visit their grandmother.
On Monday they go to school, so the day is very different!

Make the sentences negative to talk about Monday.
1) They play football.
2) They watch a film.
3) I visit my grandmother.
4) Write the short form of do not.

A pupil from the school magazine interviews Mr Mansour, the English teacher.
Pupil: (you / like) coffee?
Mr Mansour: Yes, I do. I drink coffee every morning.
Pupil: (you / get up) early?
Mr Mansour: Yes, I do. I get up at six.
Pupil: (you / play) sport?
Mr Mansour: No, I don't.

1) Write the pupil's three questions correctly.
2) Write the two short answers to a question with Do you ...?
3) Ask your friend a question with: (you / like) tea?

Amira talks about her evenings.
Amira: I study English every evening. Then I watch TV and I play with my little sister.

1) Write the he / she / it form of the verb study.
2) Write the he / she / it form of these verbs: play, watch, carry.
3) Rewrite the text about Amira. Begin with: Amira ______ English every evening. Then she ...
4) Choose: when a verb ends in consonant + y, we change y to (ies / ys).
Put in order: every morning / breakfast / I / have.
Negative question form: Does he work? → negative.
Correct the mistake: My sister watch TV every day.
Why do we use the present simple for routines?
Complete: ___ she speak English? — Yes, she ___.
Name three school subjects in English.

Read what Hana says about her hobbies.
Hana: In my free time I ______ books about animals. I also ______ football with my brother, and in the evening I ______ to music.

1) Complete Hana's text with these verbs: play / read / listen.
2) Complete with your own answer: In my free time I ______.
3) Find the odd one out: reading / swimming / ruler / drawing.

Look at the things in Karim's schoolbag: a pen, a ruler, a pencil, a dictionary, a notebook, a book.

1) Which two things do you use to write?
2) Match each thing with its use.
Things: a) ruler — b) dictionary — c) notebook
Uses: 1. to find the meaning of words — 2. to draw straight lines — 3. to write the lessons in
3) Complete with a or an: I have ______ pen, ______ pencil and ______ English book.

Read Yasmine's timetable for Monday morning.
| Time | Lesson |
|---|---|
| 8:00 | Maths |
| 9:00 | Science |
| 10:00 | English |
| 11:00 | P.E. |

Yasmine: I love experiments, so my favourite ______ is Science.

1) Complete Yasmine's sentence with one word.
2) What does Yasmine have at ten o'clock? Answer with a full sentence.
3) Find the odd one out: History / Geography / ruler / Art.
4) Write about you: My favourite subject is ______ because ______.

Read about the music club.
Selim is in the music club at school. He likes ______ (play) the guitar. His friend Aya loves ______ (sing), but she hates ______ (dance).

1) Complete the text with the correct form of the verbs in brackets.
2) Complete the rule: after like, love, enjoy and hate, we use verb + ______.
3) Write the -ing form of: read, swim, draw.
4) Write one true sentence about you with I like + verb-ing.
What is the place where we borrow books?
Name three hobbies.
Odd one out: football, tennis, pencil, swimming.

Read Bilel's short text about his hobby.
My hobby is drawing. I draw animals every weekend. I like drawing because it is relaxing.

1) What is Bilel's hobby? When does he draw?
2) Find in the text the word that gives a reason.
3) Use the notes to write two sentences about Sarra: hobby: swimming / when: every Friday.
4) Now write three sentences about your own hobby: say what it is, when you do it and why you like it.
Ask a classmate about their hobby.

Mum is looking for Wassim's things in his bedroom.
Mum: Where are your shoes, Wassim?
Wassim: They are ______ the bed, on the floor.
Mum: And where is your ball?
Wassim: It is ______ the chair.

1) Complete the dialogue with the preposition that means “below”.
2) Write the opposite of this sentence: The cat is on the table.
3) Answer with a full sentence: Where are Wassim's shoes?

Little Adam is tidying his bedroom. Read the table.
| Thing | Where? |
|---|---|
| ball | inside the box |
| toy cars | inside the box |
| books | inside the schoolbag |

1) Complete with one word: The ball is ______ the box.
2) Write a sentence about the toy cars.
3) Write a sentence about the books.
4) Choose the right words: we use “in” when a thing is (inside / on top of) another thing.

Read about the kitchen.
It is lunch time. The plates are on the table. The cat is hungry: it jumps, and now it is on top of the table too! Mother is not happy.

1) Complete with one word: The cat is ______ the table.
2) Find in the text another thing that is on the table.
3) Choose the correct word: The glass is (on / in) the shelf.
4) True or false? We use “on” when a thing is on top of another thing and touches it.
Complete: The dog is ___ of the house (front).
Complete: The garden is ___ the house (back).

Read the description of an English classroom.
Our classroom is nice. There is a big picture of London on the wall. There is also a map of Tunisia on the wall, next to the board.

1) Complete: The picture is ______ the wall.
2) Where is the map? Answer with a full sentence.
3) Choose the correct preposition: There is a poster (in / on / under) the door. — My books are (in / on) my bag.
4) Choose the reason: we say “on the wall” because the picture is (inside the wall / on the surface of the wall).

Read the description of Rania's bedroom.
My desk is near the window. My lamp is not on the desk: it is on a small table beside the desk. My bed is on the left of the desk and my chair is on the right, so the desk is in the middle.

1) Complete with two words: The lamp is ______ ______ the desk.
2) Find in the text one word that has the same meaning.
3) Complete: The desk is ______ the bed and the chair.
4) Write one sentence with next to about your classroom.
Complete: The bank is ___ the school and the shop (middle).

Malek describes his room, but he mixes up in and on.
(a) The book is in the table. (b) My ball is on the box and the box is closed. (c) There is a poster in the wall. (d) My pens are in the pencil case.

1) Three sentences have a wrong preposition. Find the correct sentence.
2) Rewrite the three wrong sentences.
3) Complete the rule: we use ______ for a surface (table, wall) and ______ for the inside of something (box, bag).
4) Write one sentence with in and one sentence with on about your schoolbag or your desk.

Read the description of Omar's place in the classroom.
I sit near the window. My bag is under my chair, next to the desk. My books are on the desk and my pens are in my pencil case. My friend Zied sits behind me.

1) List the six prepositions of place in the text.
2) Where is Omar's bag? Where are his pens? Answer with full sentences.
3) Use the notes to write one sentence: Zied's bag — on the floor — between the desk and the wall.
4) Describe where your own bag is in one sentence with two prepositions.

Look at the list of animals in Uncle Hedi's garden: one cat, two dogs, no horse, no birds.

Answer the questions with a short answer (Yes, there is. / No, there isn't. / Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.).
1) Is there a cat in the garden?
2) Is there a horse in the garden?
3) Are there two dogs in the garden?
4) Are there any birds in the garden?

Look at the things in Sami's room: one book, one lamp, one computer and one schoolbag.

Complete the sentences with There is, then answer.
1) ______ a book on the table.
2) ______ a lamp next to the computer.
3) The schoolbag is under the table. Write a sentence that begins with There is.
4) Choose the right word: we use “There is” with a (singular / plural) noun.

Read the notes about Mariem's classroom.
| Thing | Number |
|---|---|
| windows | 3 |
| door | 1 |
| desks | 15 |
| board | 1 |

Use the table to complete the sentences with There is or There are.
1) ______ three windows in the room.
2) ______ a door.
3) ______ fifteen desks.
4) Write one sentence about the board.
Complete: ___ any chairs? — No, there aren't.

Hatem is visiting the new school library. He asks the librarian some questions.

Use the words to write Hatem's questions with Is there ...? or Are there ...?
1) (books / on the shelf)
2) (a computer / in the library)
3) (dictionaries / on the table)
4) The librarian says yes to question 1 and no to question 2. Write her two short answers.

Ines writes about her grandfather's garden, but she makes mistakes with there is / there are.
My grandfather has a nice garden. (a) There are a dog in the garden. (b) There is two orange trees near the door. (c) There are a small table under the trees. (d) There are many flowers.

1) Find the three wrong sentences and the correct sentence.
2) Rewrite the wrong sentences correctly.
3) Explain your correction of sentence (a) in a few words.
Choose: There (is/are) some milk in the fridge.

Youssef is looking in his schoolbag before the English lesson.
Youssef: Oh no! There is a book in the bag and there are some pencils, but I can't find my other things!

Make these sentences negative to say what is missing.
1) There is a pen in the bag.
2) There is a ruler in the bag.
3) There are some notebooks in the bag.
4) Write the short forms of: there is not / there are not.
When do we use "there is" and "there are"?
Describe your desk using there is/are (one sentence).
The brother of your father is your ___.
Complete: This is my father. ___ name is Ali.
Complete: This is my mother. ___ name is Sana.
Complete the possessive: the book of Sami → Sami's ___.

Read about the Ben Salah family.
Mr and Mrs Ben Salah live in Nabeul. They have a big house with a garden, a red car and two cats.

Choose the correct word.
1) This is (their / theirs) house.
2) The red car is (their / theirs).
3) These are (their / theirs) cats.
4) Complete the rule with their or theirs: we use ______ before a noun, and we use ______ alone, without a noun.
The daughter of your uncle is your ___.

Nour shows a family photo to her friend. There is one mistake in each sentence.
a) This is my sister Rim and this is she book.
b) This is my brother Ali and this is he bike.
c) These are my parents and this is they car.

1) Find the wrong word in each sentence.
2) Rewrite the three sentences correctly.
3) Complete the rule: before a noun we use a ______ adjective (my, your, his, her, our, their), not a subject pronoun.

Look at the table.
| Subject | Before a noun | Alone (no noun) |
|---|---|---|
| I | my | mine |
| you | your | yours |
| we | our | ours |
| they | their | theirs |

Use the table to complete each sentence with one word.
1) This is our dog. The dog is ______. (we)
2) This is my ruler. The ruler is ______. (I)
3) These are their bikes. The bikes are ______. (they)
4) It is your pen. The pen is ______. (you)
Rewrite with possessive: the toys of the children.

Read the text about Salma's pet.
Salma has a small cat. (a) It's white and (b) its eyes are green. (c) It's very funny. Every morning the cat drinks (d) its milk in the kitchen.

1) Which forms (a, b, c, d) mean “it is”? Which forms show possession?
2) Complete with its or it's:
- Look at the bird! ______ in the tree and ______ wings are blue.
- The school is big. ______ library is new.
3) Explain the difference between its and it's in one sentence.
Complete: Where are you ___? — I am from Tunisia.
Give a formal greeting in the morning.
Complete: ___ is your name? — My name is Sami.

Read the identity cards of two pupils.
| Name | Age | City |
|---|---|---|
| Mehdi | 13 | Sfax |
| Lina | 12 | Bizerte |

1) You are Mehdi. Answer the question: How old are you?
2) You are Lina. Answer the same question.
3) Complete: Mehdi ______ thirteen years old.
4) Choose the correct sentence: I have thirteen years. / I am thirteen years old.

Read the dialogue at a family party.
Mr Jones: Good evening. My name is Tom Jones.
Mrs Karoui: Nice to meet you. I'm Leila Karoui.
Mr Jones: ______?
Mrs Karoui: I'm a doctor. I work in a hospital.

1) Write the missing question about Mrs Karoui's job. Give two possible forms.
2) Match each job with its place. Jobs: doctor, teacher, farmer. Places: school, farm, hospital.
3) Complete with a or an: She is ______ doctor. He is ______ engineer.
4) Ask your friend the same question about his or her father.

A new pupil, Farah, meets a classmate. There is one mistake in each of the classmate's questions.
Classmate: Hello! What is you name?
Farah: My name is Farah.
Classmate: And what is you family name?
Farah: It's Gharbi.
Classmate: Where is you house?
Farah: It's near the school.

1) Find the wrong word in the three questions.
2) Rewrite the three questions correctly.
3) Complete: “you” is a subject pronoun; “______” is a possessive adjective and it comes before a noun.

Two friends meet in the street.
Salim: Hi, Nader! How ______ you?
Nader: I ______ fine, thanks. And you?
Salim: I'm very well, thank you. How ______ your mother?
Nader: She ______ fine too.

1) Complete the dialogue with am, is or are.
2) Give another answer to the question “How are you?”.
3) Write the full form of: I'm.
4) Match each subject with its verb. Subjects: I, you, she. Verbs: is, am, are.

Read the dialogue at the school library.
Librarian: Good morning. What's your name?
Pupil: My name is Yassine Trabelsi.
Librarian: How do you spell your first name?
Pupil: ______

Answer the questions.
1) Write the pupil's answer: spell the name Yassine letter by letter.
2) Spell the family name Trabelsi in the same way.
3) Write the question we ask when we want to know the spelling of a word.
4) Now spell your own first name.

It is nine o'clock in the evening. Amine is at his friend Omar's house. Now he wants to go home.
Amine: It's late. I must go now. ______, Omar!
Omar: ______, Amine. See you tomorrow at school!

1) Choose the two correct expressions to complete the dialogue: Good morning / Goodbye / Good night / Hello.
2) Put each expression in the right group (when we arrive / when we leave): Hi, Bye, Good evening, See you later.
3) Write what you say to your mother before you go to bed.
Complete a self-introduction (name, age, country).
